message.content:
Lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga) belong to very different mammalian orders—Carnivora and Perissodactyla, respectively. Their most recent common ancestor is therefore a member of the larger clade **Laurasiatheria**, which gave rise to many modern mammal groups including carnivores, ungulates, bats, and whales.

That ancestor would have been a small, insectivorous or omnivorous mammal that lived roughly **70–80 million years ago** during the late Cretaceous/early Paleogene. It was not a “lion” or a “zebra” at all, but a primitive mammal that eventually split into the lineages that led to the diverse mammals we see today.
